Mr. President, in a world marked by

Every international institution beyond

Moreover, trust is an ongoing process.
Pope Leo identifies three essential
words that must guide diplomacy.
peace, justice and truth. He warns
against the return of a diplomacy of
force and reaffirms the indispensable
role of multilateral institutions.
Mr. President, the human person remains
the measure of all progress. At the
earth of this conviction start the
acknowledgment of the inviable god-given
dignity of every human person.
From this flows the sacredness of life
from conception to natural death as well
as the imperative to safeguard the human
person and that every society that
aspires to be regarded as civilized has
a duty to protect.
Publio addressed in his first encyclical
letter the new technological challenge
which he does not reject but calls for
its ethical ordering.
The control of these powerful tools must
not remain in the hands of a select few.
They must serve humanity known the other
way around.
In particular, the de development of
little autonomous weapons system raises
profound moral questions.
In this critical domain, Pope Leo
provides clear criteria for discernment.
The first concerns personal
responsibility.
The second pertains to the moral time
frame for making judgments.
The third is the protection of
civilians.
These criteria give rise to certain
non-negotiable requirements.
First of all, systems used in war
setting must guarantee the possibility
of retracing and reconstructing decision
making processes
so that accountability and blame are not
collapsed into the machine.
Second, the decision to use a little
force cannot be delegated to opaque or
automated processes but must remain
under effective self-aware and
responsible human control. Finally, it
is imperative to establish a shared
framework also at the international
level in order to curb the technological
arms race and ensure robust protection
for civilians and the infrastructures
necessary for their survival.
For some years now, the world has

At the same time, it is necessary to
consider that peace is not a negative
word. That is the mere absence of war.
Peace is first a gift, the gift of the
risen Christ, yet an active and
demanding gift. It is built in the heart
of every person and is an integral part
of the collective memory of every
community as well as humanity's heritage
in the effort of to restoring trust and
peace. Disarmament is therefore not an
optional ideal but a necessary vehicle.
No true peace is possible without
genuine common resolve for disarmament.
Mr. President,
the dignity of the person finds concrete
expression in the fundamental human
rights and freedoms which are invaluable
since they are inherent in the human
person and in human dignity.
Particular attention must to be paid to
those categories of persons most at
risk. Those in the home, the elderly,
the disabled, the sick, refugees and
migrants, the unemployed, the
marginalized, the lonely and those
living under condition of extreme
poverty, violence or conflict.
Among these fundamental rights,
religious freedom occupies a privileged
place. It is not a secondary liberty,
but an essential dimension of the human
person.
Tragically, Christians in many parts of
the world continue to suffer
discrimination,
violence, and outright persecution.
And while condemning all forms of
religious discrimination,
the Holy Sea raises its voice on behalf
of these brothers and sisters, not in a
spirit of exclusive advocacy, but
because the defense of any any of one
community's freedom strengthens the
freedom of all.
Mr. President, the passing of time does
not make a war any less intolerable.
Rather, it makes the responsibility of
those who can end or help bring it to an
end all the more grave. After more than
four years of war in Ukraine, the death

tragedy, the Holy Sea, while calling for
strict observance of the international
humanitarian law, highlights the urgent
necessity to bring hostilities to an end
and paving way for diplomacy.
The Holy Sea encourages every initiative
aimed at achieving an immediate,
complete, and effective ceasefire.

The OIC is following with deep concern
the situation in the Gulf region where

In particular, the holy sea cannot

The holy sea strongly reiterates its

The international community must not

These individuals are deprived of their
inherent rights in fragrant disrespect
of their human dignity.
Their suffering must end. The condition
must be created within their homeland to
allow the safe, legal, voluntary, and
unhindered return.

Mr. President, the transformation the
world is facing technological,
geopolitical, social will not wait for
the activity or inactivity of the United
Nations. Whether it becomes a
transformation that elevates the human
person or one that diminishes it depends
on the choices made together in these
rooms. It is imperative to desire not
only weapons but the logic of
domination, to protect the most in need,
to speak the truth in charity, and to
rebuild through dialogue and solidarity
a multilateral order that truly delivers
for all.
May the international community as the
family of nations have the courage to
restore trust, the wisdom to manage
transformation justly and the
perseverance to build peace. In this
regard, the holy sea strongly urges all
parties to engage in sincere negotiation
to put an end to all wars and conflicts.
War brings only death and destruction,
whereas peace brings development and
prosperity.
The Holy Sea will continue to play its
part in building a better future for
all. Thank you.
